chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen narrated from his brother Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father, from Abu al-Hasan (the preceding Imam), peace be upon him, who said:

I asked him about a man who said to his wife or his concubine — in Mina — after he had shaved his head and had not yet performed Tawaf around the House and had not yet performed Sa'i, 'Throw off your garment,' and he looked at her private part. He said: 'There is no penalty upon him if it was not more than looking.'

key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina, a location central to Hajj rituals
key_terms.حَلَقَ: He shaved (his head, indicating partial exit from Ihram)
key_terms.سَعَى: Performed Sa'i between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Penalty/Expiation (implied by context of 'la shay' ala-hi')

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim who looks at his wife's private part in Mina after shaving but before completing Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the distinction between minor and major breaches of Ihram rituals, specifically addressing the penalty for a pilgrim who looks at his wife’s private part in Mina after shaving but before completing Tawaf and Sa'i. The ruling emphasizes that mere visual inspection incurs no kaffarah, highlighting the Shia jurisprudential principle of differentiating between simple negligence and substantive ritual invalidation. This serves as a practical guide for pilgrims regarding the graduated nature of penalties in Hajj obligations.
